# The engine's tear-out flashes the UA default because it never passes the stagedColorScheme its own Main API accepts

`Serves:` #18304 — one of the two seams that epic's [seam account](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5563564532) identified as belonging in the engine, narrowed to its actionable half by the [mechanism correction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5564009259).

## Context

`Main.windowOpen` opens a **blank same-origin staging document** before navigating to the real URL, so the child can connect to the shared worker while the opener is warm. That staging realm paints before the app exists, so its colour is whatever the platform defaults to.

The parameter that fixes this already exists and has for some time — `Main.mjs:1175`:

```js
windowOpen({nativeCapabilities, stagedColorScheme, topologyIdentity=null, url, useTotalHeight=true, windowFeatures, windowName})
```

`Main.mjs:1206-1211` writes it onto the staging document as a `color-scheme` meta.

## The Problem

Exactly one caller passes it.

| caller | passes `stagedColorScheme` |
|---|---|
| `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:2507` | **yes** — `schemes[selectedTheme]` |
| `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs#openTearOutVessel` | **no** |

So a tear-out driven by the **engine** flashes the user-agent default before the pane appears, and the same gesture in `apps/workstation` does not — because that app built the compensation itself.

This is the same shape as every other finding in #18304's seam account: the capability exists, the engine does not use it, and the consumer supplies what the engine did not. It is the reason the account lists `openTearOutVessel` as an engine gap rather than as app policy.

## The Architectural Reality

The [author's pre-implementation correction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18432#issuecomment-5564176451) supersedes the original worker-side map prescription. The schemes already exist in component theme declarations, and the value is needed by `Main.windowOpen` on the main thread where computed CSS is available.

## The Fix

Declare `--neo-color-scheme` in each theme's `Global.scss`. `Main.windowOpen` defaults an omitted `stagedColorScheme` through `resolveThemeColorScheme()`, reading the themed document element. The existing explicit caller value wins; an absent or invalid declaration yields `undefined` and preserves the existing platform fallback. No theme-name parsing or new worker payload is required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `Main.windowOpen` defaults `stagedColorScheme` from the live document's declared theme scheme when the caller supplies none.
- [ ] AC-2: an undeclared or unknown theme supplies no scheme; no value is guessed.
- [ ] AC-3: no theme-name parsing anywhere in the path. `theme-cyberpunk` declares `dark` despite its name.
- [ ] AC-4: Workstation's existing explicit `schemes[selectedTheme]` path remains unchanged and wins.

## Constraints

Declared, never inferred. The engine tear-out caller needs no change; the main-thread staging owner resolves the default. The eventual vessel app theme remains outside this ticket under #18304, as does consolidating component-level color-scheme declarations onto this token.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Main.windowOpen` / `stagedColorScheme` | Existing staging API and author's AC revision | Explicit caller value wins; omitted value defaults from live theme declaration | No admitted scheme means no staging meta | `windowOpen` JSDoc | Computed-style component case and call-boundary probe |
| `--neo-color-scheme` / `Main.resolveThemeColorScheme` | Theme Global.scss declarations | Read declared dark/light from the themed document element | Unknown, absent, or invalid declaration yields undefined | Reader JSDoc and theme tokens | Five theme declarations; live dark/light and absence controls |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — preserves the staging parameter, adds its document-owned default, and introduces no worker wire change.

## Prior art

#18414 / PR #18418 is the sibling half of the same missing capability, reached from the other end: the cross-window placeholder rendered black-on-white under every theme because nothing carried theme values across the tear-out boundary. Two independent defects, one gap.

Filed by @neo-opus-grace (Claude Opus 5), origin session `70502f9a-5b14-4dcf-bcdf-4a29b546df77`.


## Timeline

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-07T02:24:10Z

## The fix I specified is bigger and worse than the one the evidence points at — revising AC-1 before implementing

Two measurements changed the shape.

### 1. Every theme already declares a scheme, and they already agree

I filed this saying the engine has no theme→scheme map. It has no *theme-level* one — but the themes already declare the value per component, and they are unanimous:

| theme | declared scheme | declarations |
|---|---|---|
| `neo-dark` | dark | 4 |
| `neo-light` | light | 4 |
| `dark` | dark | 3 |
| `light` | light | 3 |
| `cyberpunk` | **dark** | 2 |

Sixteen declarations across five themes, **zero disagreement**. So the fact exists in the substrate; it simply has no single name.

This also settles the ticket's central constraint **empirically rather than by assertion**: `theme-cyberpunk` declares `dark` while being named neither. A name-derived scheme is wrong for one of the five themes we ship today, not hypothetically one day.

### 2. The value is needed on the main thread, where the theme already is

`stagedColorScheme` is consumed by `Main.windowOpen` (`Main.mjs:1206-1211`), which runs on the **main thread**, against a document that already carries the theme class. My AC-1 had the app worker plumb a value it cannot read — a CSS custom property is not reachable from the worker, so that design implies a round trip to fetch a fact the destination already has.

### Revised shape — smaller, and it removes the engine-side map entirely

- Declare `--neo-theme-color-scheme` **once per theme** (five lines), naming what those sixteen declarations already agree on.
- `Main.windowOpen` **defaults** `stagedColorScheme` from the live document when the caller supplies none.
- Every existing caller is unaffected: `apps/workstation:2507` passes an explicit value and keeps winning.
- An undeclared theme yields an empty string ⇒ pass nothing ⇒ today's behaviour, exactly as AC-2 required.

The engine's `openTearOutVessel` then needs **no change at all**. It becomes correct because the layer that owns the document resolves the fact, instead of a layer that cannot see it forwarding a fact it had to be told.

### AC revision

- **AC-1 replaced:** ~~`openTearOutVessel` passes `stagedColorScheme`~~ → **`Main.windowOpen` defaults `stagedColorScheme` from the live document's declared theme scheme when the caller supplies none.**
- **AC-2 unchanged** and now cheaper: an undeclared theme resolves to `''` and the parameter is omitted.
- **AC-3 unchanged and strengthened:** still no name parsing, and `theme-cyberpunk` is now a *measured* falsifier rather than a predicted one.
- **AC-4 unchanged:** Workstation's explicit path still wins.

### Deliberately out of scope

Collapsing the sixteen component-level declarations onto the new token. It is a real consolidation and a genuine net reduction, but it is a themes-wide refactor and this ticket is a tear-out defect. Recorded so the next person sees it was noticed and declined, not missed.
